$comment: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN THE FIXTURES AND THE FLEET. `clean` must produce nothing on every lane;
`dirty` must produce at least the findings enumerated below. Both directions matter and they
fail differently: a clean fixture that starts reporting is a FALSE POSITIVE, and a dirty
fixture that stops reporting is a FALSE NEGATIVE — the second is silent and is the one this
`mustMatch` is what keeps the fixture honest. A planted defect that gets tidied away by a
future edit would turn the dirty canary clean, and every lane would then pass by finding
nothing in a file with nothing to find. The test asserts these strings are still present
BEFORE it believes any scanner result about them.

clean.rationale: Absence of evidence is only evidence of absence if the instrument was pointed at something. This is the something.

dirty.supportNote: Files that belong to a planted artefact and carry no needle of their own. A SavedModel is a directory — saved_model.pb plus variables/ and fingerprint.pb — and only saved_model.pb holds the planted ops. Listed so the reverse walk can tell an undeclared defect from a declared plant's furniture; every entry must exist, and a file listed here may not also be a plant.

$comment: These fixtures must NOT count toward commitwork's own posture — a repository that plants
eleven defects in itself and then reports eleven findings has told you nothing. They are
excluded from the repo-wide scan and reached only by the canary test, which points the
scanners at them explicitly. Excluding them from the self-scan is not suppression: the
findings are asserted somewhere, which is the whole difference.

None of these exclusions has been verified by RUNNING the lane and diffing the finding count. They are declared, not demonstrated — which is the same gap this fixture exists to close, one level up.

knownScopeGaps.want: IN SCOPE. The root composite Action (uses: Portll/commitwork@v0.5.0) runs on other repositories' runners with their tokens, so its script injection and pinning are exactly what zizmor audits. Today it is checked only by its own unit test (bin/test/github-action.test.mjs: SHA pins, no inputs interpolated into run:, trust off by default).
knownScopeGaps.blockedBy: The bounded command passes directories only. A file argument for action.yml would make zizmor fail on every repository without one, and this bound test reads only directory arguments. Needs the command to add action.yml when it exists and the test to read file arguments, landed together.

knownScopeGaps.want: IN SCOPE. This is the negative control for the CI lane; zizmor staying quiet about a real workflow is the only thing separating 'nothing wrong' from 'nothing scanned'. Its silence is currently ASSUMED, which is the weaker of the two directions.
knownScopeGaps.blockedBy: Needs fixtures/scan-canary/clean/.github/ added to checks[actions-zizmor].local in manifests/security-baseline.json. Written there twice on 2026-09-02 and swept both times by peers committing that file before the coupled test could land with it.

knownScopeGaps.want: OUT OF SCOPE, permanently. Plants pull_request_target, permissions:write-all and an unpinned action ref so the lane can be shown to fire; counting them would report a fixture built to produce findings as this repository having them.
knownScopeGaps.blockedBy: Belongs in that check's scopeNotes as 'MINUS <path> — <why>'. Same manifest, same contention. Recorded here so the exclusion is at least DECLARED somewhere its owner can commit.
